avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Senna causes potassium depletion through increased colonic fluid loss; concurrent supplementation may create electrolyte imbalance
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor serum potassium levels; avoid routine potassium supplementation unless specifically prescribed by healthcare provider

avoid_supplements.name: Other stimulant laxatives
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive bowel stimulation and electrolyte depletion with concurrent use
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine with other stimulant laxatives; allow adequate spacing between products

caution_supplements.name: Licorice
caution_supplements.mechanism: Both licorice and senna may cause potassium depletion and sodium retention
caution_supplements.action: Monitor electrolytes if concurrent use; counsel on signs of hypokalemia

caution_supplements.name: Herbs with laxative properties (Aloe, Cascara)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive laxative effects and potential electrolyte disturbances
caution_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or space dosing; monitor bowel function and hydration status

avoid_foods.name: Excessive dietary fiber
avoid_foods.mechanism: Combined with senna's stimulant effect may cause severe cramping, diarrhea, and dehydration
avoid_foods.action: Counsel to maintain moderate fiber intake during senna use; ensure adequate fluid intake

caution_foods.name: High sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Senna-induced potassium loss may be exacerbated by high sodium intake, increasing electrolyte imbalance
caution_foods.action: Encourage moderate sodium intake and adequate hydration with senna use

monitoring_notes: Monitor for signs of chronic use complications including electrolyte depletion (hypokalemia, hyponatremia), dehydration, and potential laxative dependence. Senna should be used short-term (7-10 days maximum) unless medically indicated; assess kidney function and baseline electrolytes in elderly or high-risk patients.
